question: What are Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each currently guiding for capital expenditures, and how do they line up on a calendar-2026 basis?
grading: Reference-free recency: use each company’s latest guide before the run timestamp, date it and preserve its calendar/fiscal and lease definitions. At the October 1 snapshot, CY2026: Alphabet $195–205B; Meta $130–145B including finance-lease principal; Amazon ~$220B cash capex; Microsoft ~$175B including finance leases/excluding operating leases. Do not treat Microsoft’s fiscal FY2027 or Q1 figures as calendar totals, or invent a harmonized cash basis.
answer: As of October 1, 2026, all four provide calendar-2026 capex numbers: Alphabet USD 195–205 billion (July 22 Q2 call); [G28-E1] Meta USD 130–145 billion including finance-lease principal payments (July 29 Q2 release); [G28-E2] Amazon approximately USD 220 billion in cash capex (July 30 Q2 call); [G28-E3] Microsoft approximately USD 175 billion (July 29 FY2026 Q4 call), including finance leases but excluding operating leases. Microsoft lowered the displayed capex amount because extending building useful lives shifts some future leases to operating classification; investment expectations apart from that change were unchanged. [G28-E4] Nominal ordering is Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, but the lease definitions differ, so these are not fully harmonized cash-spending measures. Microsoft separately expects FY2027 capex to grow YoY and Q1 FY2027 capex above USD 50 billion; those fiscal guides are not additional CY2026 totals. [G28-E4]

output.answer:
**Question:** What are Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each currently guiding for capital expenditures, and how do they line up on a calendar-2026 basis?
*As of 2026-10-01*

| | Capex guidance (USD) |
|---|---|
| Alphabet — calendar 2026 (FY2026, year ending Dec 31, 2026) | $180-$190 billion [1] |
| Meta — calendar 2026 (FY2026, year ending Dec 31, 2026) | $130-145 billion [2] |
| Amazon — calendar 2026 (FY2026, year ending Dec 31, 2026) | Not disclosed in evidence [3] |
| Microsoft — calendar 2026 (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2026; spans Q3 FY2026–Q2 FY2027) | approximately $175 billion [4] |
| Microsoft — Q1 FY2027 (quarter ending Sep 30, 2026) | over $50 billion [4] |

- Meta guides calendar 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to a range of $130-145 billion, narrowed from its prior outlook of $125-145 billion. [2]
- Alphabet's 2026 capital expenditure range is $180-$190 billion, as reported by Zacks Investment Research (published via Yahoo Finance), a secondary source; Alphabet's own Q2 FY2026 release (quarter ended June 30, 2026) does not contain a capex guidance figure. [1]
- Microsoft expects calendar 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $175 billion, per CFO commentary on the Q4 FY2026 earnings call (secondary transcript), after the shift from finance to operating leases. [4]
- Microsoft guides Q1 FY2027 (quarter ending September 30, 2026) capital expenditures to over $50 billion, including the lease reclassification impact from the useful life update. [4]
- Microsoft expects FY2027 capital expenditures to grow year-over-year, given demand signals across its portfolio. [4]
- Microsoft's calendar 2026 capex guidance was mechanically reduced from the $190 billion figure disclosed in Q3 FY2026 to approximately $175 billion because the useful-life change reclassifies some leases from finance to operating leases, as reported by MLQ News, a secondary source. [5]
- Microsoft's roughly $190 billion calendar 2026 capex figure was guided in its fiscal third quarter ended March 31, 2026, per Zacks Investment Research (published via Yahoo Finance), a secondary source. [1]

**Not available**
- Amazon calendar 2026 capital expenditure guidance: Amazon's Q2 FY2026 release (quarter ended June 30, 2026) provides forward guidance only for Q3 2026 net sales and operating income; no numeric capex guidance for 2026 appears in the evidence. [3]
- Microsoft Q2 FY2027 (Oct-Dec 2026) capital expenditure guidance: Microsoft guides capex one quarter at a time; Q1 FY2027 (ended September 30, 2026) results had not been released as of 2026-10-01, so no Q2 FY2027 capex guidance has been issued. [4]

**Sources**
[1] Oracle Solidifies AI Infrastructure Positioning: Will it Drive Growth? (finance.yahoo.com, undated, secondary) https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oracle-solidifies-ai-infrastructure-positioning-161500050.html
[2] Meta Platforms, Inc. earnings release for Q2 FY2026, 8-K EX-99.1 (filed 2026-07-29) (www.sec.gov, 2026-07-29, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026050596/meta-06302026xexhibit991.htm
[3] AMAZON COM INC earnings release for Q2 FY2026, 8-K EX-99.1 (filed 2026-07-30) (www.sec.gov, 2026-07-30, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm
[4] Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) Q4 FY2026 earnings call transcript (finance.yahoo.com, undated, secondary) https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT/earnings/MSFT-Q4-2026-earnings_call-647770.html
[5] Microsoft Brought 88 Data Centers Online in FY2026, Spent $41B in Q4 Alone | MLQ News (mlq.ai, undated, secondary) https://mlq.ai/news/microsoft-brought-88-data-centers-online-in-fy2026-spent-41b-in-q4-alone
